extracted.intended_audience: Professionals and practitioners seeking to improve patent drafting skills (patent agents, agent candidates, TTO staff, TISCs staff, inventors, researchers, and others supporting inventors).
extracted.subtask_description: A practice-oriented WIPO training program (online + Geneva workshop + mentoring) teaching skills to prepare and file patent applications, with emphasis on claim and specification drafting across technology areas and jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: educational and professional prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have a Bachelor’s level degree in law, and/or in science and technology (engineering, agriculture, environmental, ICT, life sciences, medicine, physics, chemistry, communication sciences, biology, or biotechnology). OR at least 1 year of professional/work or research experience in patent drafting or patent prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also requires general knowledge of IP and patents at least equivalent to WIPO Academy DL301 - Advanced Course on Patents; proficiency in written and spoken English (completed degree in English OR TOEFL iBT 80/120 OR IELTS 6.5/9 in last 3 years). Applicants submit online application and supporting documents; WIPO selects a limited number on a rolling basis; limited scholarships available for least developed/developing/transition economies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim drafting techniques and methodologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn claim drafting techniques and methodologies aimed at drafting the all-important claims that determine the scope and coverage of protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical exercises and personal feedback are used to develop the capacity to formulate credible sets of claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification drafting (description, summary, background/abstract)
rubrics_metrics.description: Training covers drafting the specification including the description, summary and background/abstract for inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tutor-led modules and practical exercises focus on drafting clear, complete specifications that support claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis of inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants learn how to analyse inventions to identify inventive features and draftable subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis skills feed into claim and specification drafting exercises and strategic filing decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic filing decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The program addresses strategic decisions around filing (e.g., scope of protection, jurisdictions, timing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curriculum is designed to give participants an edge when transforming ideas into solid global patent portfolios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hands-on experiential learning and personal feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: The Training Program offers hands-on experiential learning delivered by globally recognized instructors where practical exercises and personal feedback are the main learning instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State-of-the-art WIPO e-learning tools, theme-based discussion forums, individual feedback and mentoring are used; face-to-face workshop in Geneva supplements online work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposure to international patent practice
rubrics_metrics.description: A curriculum specifically designed for exposure to international patent practice to prepare participants for drafting across jurisdictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes modules and workshop sessions on drafting for different jurisdictions and strategic drafting in specific technology areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 1 — Drafting basics (modules & outcomes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fundamentals of drafting claims and the specification via tutor-led study of online modules: Fundamentals of Patent Drafting, Parts of a Patent Application, Relevance of Claim Drafting: Types of claims, Designing claims, Drafting a Description, Performing Drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants complete practical exercises to assess background and description of inventions and formulate credible sets of claims and specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 2 — Geneva workshop topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshop sessions cover: Fundamentals of Patent Law and Specification Structure; Making the Most Out of the Inventor Interview; An Expert Approach to Claim Drafting – Functional Analysis; Strategic Drafting in Specific Technology Areas; Drafting for Different Jurisdictions; Thinking Ahead: Drafting Enforceable Claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Face-to-face workshop combines theory and practice to develop skills in drafting claims and specifications covering a comprehensive scope of protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 3 — Mentoring and advanced exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow-up mentoring focused on reinforcing skills from Phases 1 and 2 through advanced patent drafting exercises and discussions tailored to participants' technical fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expert-guided practical exercises include: Claim Drafting in View of Prior Art; Amending Claims and Draft Specification; Claim Drafting for Chemistry/Biology; Claim Drafting for Electronics/Mechanics; direct interaction and hands-on advice from instructors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment and certification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A WIPO Certificate is awarded to those who successfully complete Phases 1, 2 and 3 of the training program and pass the Evaluations scheduled at the end of the training program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completion is contingent on attending all phases and passing scheduled evaluations (details on evaluation format not specified on page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: The program is offered in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proficiency in written and spoken English is required (see eligibility for acceptable proof).

rubrics_metrics.name: Target participants / who should apply
rubrics_metrics.description: Intended for patent agents and patent agent candidates; staff of technology transfer offices and WIPO TISCs; others regularly involved in supporting inventors; innovators, researchers and public members wishing to enhance patent drafting skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program is practice-oriented and suitable for those with professional or commercial interest in patents across different technical fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical outcome: ability to draft enforceable, comprehensive protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants should gain the capacity to draft enforceable claims and specifications that provide a comprehensive scope of protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on drafting enforceable claims, functional analysis, anticipating jurisdictional differences, and thinking ahead to enforceability.
